lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When cities plan new trees, the conversation usually focuses on appearance. But the more interesting argument is about temperature. On a summer afternoon, a street with a full canopy of trees can be several degrees cooler than a similar street without them, partly because of shade and partly because trees release water through their leaves. Now, there's a catch. Trees planted today will take ten to twenty years to provide that benefit, and many young trees die in their first few summers because nobody waters them. So some cities have started paying residents a small amount to look after the tree outside their home. Early results are encouraging, although it's too soon to say whether people will keep it up once the novelty wears off.
